//: A version per RELEASE CADENCE, because the four deployables do not ship on
the same clock and a shared counter would be driven entirely by the fastest
api/web deploy continuously — many times a day, always together, from the
same commit. android/ios ship through store review every few weeks. Under a
single product version the repo would read 0.9.0 while the App Store still
served 0.1.0: not a shared version at all, just a misleading one, with the
mobile source tree claiming a version no user is running.
release-please routes each commit to a package by the FILES it touches, so an
api-only change bumps only api and never disturbs the mobile versions. That
is the whole point: nothing is 'released' unless its own files changed.
Build NUMBERS stay out of this — versionCode and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION come
from the git commit count at build time (monotonic by construction, see
mobile.yml). This owns only the human-facing versions.
One PR covers every pending bump (separate-pull-requests: false), so there is
still only one thing to merge.
